Updated: 2026-10-16 · Measured Xu v0.8.11 · Dual-Architecture (ARM64 + x86_64)

Multi-Architecture Cross-Language Benchmarks

Rigorous, reproducible cross-language benchmarks comparing Xu v0.8.11 against C (best Clang O1–O3), Rust (best rustc O1–O3), Swift (swiftc -O), and Go (go build) across 47 measured workloads. Concurrently verified across dual architectures (ARM64 & x86_64) on macOS, Linux, and Windows.

Openness & Transparency Charter

Unbiased, 100% Transparent Cross-Language Benchmarks

Every benchmark runs fully automated inside GitHub Actions cloud runners across physical and isolated OS environments. Test implementations, compilation flags, execution environments, and raw metrics are 100% open-source and publicly auditable. We eliminate cherry-picked data, artificial optimizations, and black-box measurements.

Automated CI: GitHub Actions Compiler Bootstrap Verified: Gen2 = Gen3 Source Actions Run (afd05ca35f5d6c270f4415af807fece5ce64bba8) github.com/xulang-org/bench Raw Dataset: benchmarks.json

100% Open-Source Implementations

Full implementations of all 13 workloads across Xu, C, Rust, Go, and Swift are publicly accessible. Inspect isomorphic algorithm structure instantly with the in-page 'View Source' modal or browse on GitHub.

Strict Isomorphic Workloads & No Bias

Workloads strictly share equivalent algorithmic logic and data structures. No hand-tuned assembly hacks or specialized compiler cheating. C and Rust automatically select the lowest measured median among O1–O3.

Automated Dual-Arch 6-Platform CI

Concurrently measured across macOS, Linux, and Windows on both ARM64 and x86_64 architectures. Every data point is generated in cloud runners without manual local machine selection.

7-Run Median & Open Dataset

Seven independent whole-program executions per implementation; wall time uses the median, accounting for cold launch overhead. Peak RSS and unstripped binary size are reported faithfully with full JSON datasets.

Language Engineering Profiles & Trade-offs

Design Trade-offs

Synthesizing all 6 architecture platforms and 47 audited workloads across execution speed, RSS memory, binary size, and CPU efficiency:

🔵 C (Clang / GCC -O3) Direct Hardware Mapping · Zero Runtime

Direct mapping to machine instructions with zero language runtime overhead. Serves as the industry gold standard for wall time, CPU efficiency, and compact binary footprint.

🟠 Rust (rustc -O3) Ownership Model · Zero-Cost Abstractions

Compile-time borrow checking provides type-safe memory management without garbage collection. Delivers top-tier compute performance; standalone binaries embed the standard library on static linking targets.

🟣 Xu AOT Compilation · Deterministic Zero-GC

Adopts deterministic scope-based destruction and compile-time borrowing without a tracing garbage collector. Delivers sub-millisecond startup, tight RSS footprint (0.5–4MB), and compact binaries (20–70KB) with near-C/Rust compute throughput.

🌸 Swift (swiftc -O) Modern Expressive · Auto ARC

Combines expressive modern syntax with LLVM backend optimization for robust compute throughput. Manages memory via ARC, where atomic reference adjustments and standard runtime establish a baseline footprint.

🟢 Go (gc) CSP Concurrency · Low-Latency Concurrent GC

Renowned for fast compilation, developer velocity, and native Goroutine/Channel concurrency. Embeds a concurrent tri-color GC and cross-platform scheduler, trading runtime baseline footprint for robust concurrent engineering ergonomics.

Memory Footprint & Binary Size (All Platforms & Languages)

All Peers Compared

Each cell spans different workloads, not a matched-workload memory ranking. Linux peak RSS is collected in a separate post-exec run; tracing is excluded from wall time. macOS uses wait4 and Windows uses peak working set; these OS accounting methods differ.

Audited Methodology & Execution Environment

Seven whole-program executions per implementation; reported wall time is the median including process launch. C and Rust select the lowest measured median among O1/O2/O3. Linux peak RSS is collected in a separate post-exec run; tracing is excluded from wall time. macOS uses wait4 and Windows uses peak working set; these OS accounting methods differ. All Xu outputs and exit codes passed harness verification. Compiler identities, source closures and Gen2=Gen3 bootstrap verified.

Audited Platform & Telemetry Matrix
Target PlatformArchitectureMemory & Time Accounting
macOS ARM64Apple Silicon (M-series)wait4: whole-process peak RSS & CPU time
Linux ARM64ARM64 (Ubuntu Cloud)post-exec address space peak RSS (tracing excluded)
Windows ARM64ARM64 (Windows Server)OS Job Object: Peak Working Set memory
macOS x86_64Intel Core x86_64wait4: whole-process peak RSS & CPU time
Linux x86_64AMD64 / x86_64 (Ubuntu Cloud)post-exec address space peak RSS (tracing excluded)
Windows x86_64AMD64 / x86_64 (Windows Server)OS Job Object: Peak Working Set memory
